Are you facing legal issues in Pierce County, Washington, and need to navigate the court system? This article provides a comprehensive guide to Pierce County Superior Court, including its history, functions, and services. Whether you're a resident or visitor, this guide will help you understand how the court operates and what you can expect.

What is Pierce County Superior Court?

Pierce County Superior Court is the highest trial court in Pierce County, Washington. The court has original jurisdiction over felony criminal cases, civil cases with a value over $100,000, family law cases, probate and guardianship matters, and juvenile offender cases. The court also hears appeals from lower courts and administrative agencies.

History of Pierce County Superior Court

Pierce County Superior Court was established in 1854, shortly after the creation of Pierce County. The first courthouse was built in Steilacoom and later moved to Tacoma in 1877. The current courthouse was constructed in 1958 and expanded in 1987 to accommodate the growing population and caseload.

Court Jurisdiction and Divisions

Pierce County Superior Court is divided into several divisions, including criminal, civil, family law, probate and guardianship, and juvenile offender. Each division has its own judges, staff, and procedures. The court also has a specialized drug court and mental health court to address specific needs of defendants.

Types of Cases Heard in Pierce County Superior Court

Pierce County Superior Court hears a wide range of cases, including:

  • Felony criminal cases, such as murder, assault, and robbery
  • Civil cases with a value over $100,000, such as personal injury, contract disputes, and property disputes
  • Family law cases, such as divorce, child custody, and adoption
  • Probate and guardianship matters, such as estate administration and conservatorship
  • Juvenile offender cases, such as delinquency and dependency

Filing a Case in Pierce County Superior Court

To file a case in Pierce County Superior Court, you must first determine which division and type of case is appropriate. You can then complete the necessary forms and pay the filing fee, which varies depending on the type of case. The court also offers electronic filing and payment options for certain cases.

Court Procedures and Processes

Pierce County Superior Court has specific procedures and processes for each division and type of case. These may include pre-trial conferences, discovery, motions, trial, and appeals. It's important to follow these procedures and comply with court rules and deadlines to avoid delays or penalties.

Legal Assistance in Pierce County Superior Court

If you cannot afford an attorney, Pierce County Superior Court provides legal assistance through the Pierce County Bar Association's Volunteer Legal Services Program and the Northwest Justice Project. The court also has a self-help center to assist with forms, procedures, and resources.

Court Records and Case Search

Pierce County Superior Court maintains records of all cases filed and heard in the court. These records are available for public access and can be searched online through the court's website or in person at the clerk's office. The court also provides copies of court documents upon request, subject to certain fees.

Jury Duty in Pierce County Superior Court

If you are a resident of Pierce County, you may be summoned for jury duty in Pierce County Superior Court. The court randomly selects potential jurors from voter registration and driver's license records. Jurors play a critical role in the justice system and must be available to serve during the term of their summons.

Court Facilities and Accessibility

Pierce County Superior Court is located in downtown Tacoma and has several facilities, including the main courthouse, juvenile court, and family court. The court has accessible entrances, parking, and restrooms for individuals with disabilities. The court also provides language interpreters and accommodations for individuals with special needs.

Court Rules and Policies

Pierce County Superior Court has specific rules and policies for conduct in the court, including dress code, cell phone use, and prohibited items. The court also has policies for media access, cameras, and recordings. It's important to review these rules and policies before entering the court to avoid disruptions or penalties.

Court Fees and Payments

Pierce County Superior Court charges fees for filing and other court services, such as copies and transcripts. The court accepts payments by cash, check, credit card, and electronic means. The court also offers fee waivers for individuals who meet certain income and hardship requirements.

Contacting Pierce County Superior Court

If you need to contact Pierce County Superior Court, you can visit the court's website or contact the clerk's office by phone, email, or mail. The court also has a customer service center to assist with general inquiries and referrals to court services.

Pierce County Superior Court Records

Pierce County Superior Court maintains records of all cases heard in the court. These records are available to the public, and individuals can access them by visiting the clerk's office or by requesting them online through the court's website. Court records contain information about the parties involved in the case, the charges or claims made, and the outcome of the case.

Pierce County Superior Court LINX

Pierce County Superior Court LINX is an online system that allows individuals to access court records, file court documents, and make payments. The system is available 24/7 and provides convenient access to court information from anywhere with an internet connection. To use LINX, individuals must create an account and pay a one-time registration fee.

Pierce County Superior Court Case Search

Pierce County Superior Court provides a case search function on its website. Individuals can search for cases by party name, case number, or hearing date. The search results will provide information about the case, including the parties involved, the charges or claims made, and the status of the case.

Pierce County Superior Court Live Stream

Pierce County Superior Court provides live streaming of court proceedings for public viewing. The live stream can be accessed through the court's website and allows individuals to observe court proceedings remotely. Live streaming provides increased transparency and accessibility to the court system.

Pierce County Superior Court Rules

Pierce County Superior Court has specific rules and policies for conduct in the court, including dress code, cell phone use, and prohibited items. The court also has rules for filing documents, serving process, and conducting hearings. It's important to review these rules and policies before entering the court to avoid disruptions or penalties.

Pierce County Superior Court Judges

Pierce County Superior Court has several judges who preside over cases heard in the court. Judges are appointed by the governor and serve for six years. The judges are responsible for ensuring that court proceedings are fair and impartial and that the law is followed.

Pierce County Superior Court E-Filing

Pierce County Superior Court accepts electronic filing of court documents through its LINX system. E-filing allows individuals to file documents without visiting the court in person and provides a more efficient and streamlined process. However, there are specific rules and procedures that must be followed for e-filing, and not all documents can be filed electronically.

Conclusion

Pierce County Superior Court plays a vital role in the justice system of Pierce County, Washington. Whether you're involved in a legal matter or simply want to learn more about the court, this guide provides a comprehensive overview of the court's history, functions, and services. Remember to follow court rules and procedures, seek legal assistance if necessary, and fulfill your responsibilities as a juror if summoned.
